metadata.title: FrontlineAI - 100 Clinically Grounded Health-Worker Questions & Answers
metadata.subtitle: Papua New Guinea / WHO source-of-truth benchmark compiled from the 14 supplied clinical documents
metadata.purpose: This is a source-grounded benchmark for evaluating a clinical AI/RAG system and for training/QA discussion. It is not a replacement for bedside assessment, current national policy, specialist advice, or local escalation pathways. Where the supplied documents conflict, newer and more specific guidance should take precedence. In particular, the 2021 paediatric ART updates supersede older HIV first-line details, and the 2022 WHO child/adolescent TB handbook is preferred over older TB material.
metadata.design: The questions are written in simple, practical language similar to what nurses, HEOs, CHWs and doctors may ask. Answers are deliberately concise and auditable. Each answer names the source document and page/section used.
metadata.source_hierarchy: 1) Newer PNG/WHO updates for the exact topic; 2) PNG national standard-treatment guidance for local practice; 3) WHO technical guidance; 4) older PNG textbooks mainly as supporting context. The older 2003 paediatrics text was not allowed to override later treatment guidance.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Emergency triage signs. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: Obstructed or absent breathing, severe respiratory distress, central cyanosis, shock, coma/reduced consciousness, convulsions, or severe dehydration with diarrhoea require immediate emergency treatment.
questions.source_of_truth: WHO Pocket Book of Hospital Care for Children (2013), pp. 2-4.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Sick infant priority. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: Any sick infant under 2 months is a priority patient and should be assessed without unnecessary delay.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Young-infant danger signs. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: For infants under 2 months, danger signs include inability to suck/feed, RR >60/min, RR <20/min or apnoea, severe chest indrawing, central cyanosis, and very cold arms/legs.
questions.source_of_truth: PNG Standard Treatment for Common Illnesses of Children (2016), p. 13.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Oxygen threshold. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: In most children, oxygen is indicated when SpO2 is below 90%, while considering altitude and clinical context.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Clinical signs of hypoxaemia. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: If oximetry is unavailable, central cyanosis, nasal flaring, inability to drink/feed due to respiratory distress, grunting every breath and depressed mental state support oxygen use; severe indrawing, RR >=70/min or head nodding may also indicate need.
questions.source_of_truth: WHO Oxygen Therapy for Children (2016), pp. 9-10, 15.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: When to consider CPAP. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: Consider CPAP when severe respiratory distress persists despite oxygen or severe hypoxaemia persists, especially SpO2 <85% despite high-flow oxygen.
questions.source_of_truth: Bubble-CPAP Guidelines (2017), pp. 2-3.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Small baby care. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: For babies under 2.2 kg: keep warm, preferably skin-to-skin/KMC, and start breastfeeds within about 30-60 minutes; use expressed breast milk if sucking is poor.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Neonatal infection signs. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: Possible neonatal infection signs include fever/hypothermia, poor suck, distension, vomiting all feeds, fits, pustules, jaundice, infected cord, RR >60, apnoea, severe indrawing, cyanosis, prolonged membrane rupture, maternal fever or offensive liquor.
questions.source_of_truth: PNG Standard Treatment Book (2016), p. 28.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Neonatal antibiotics. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: The PNG manual uses ampicillin (or penicillin/crystapen) plus gentamicin as initial treatment for suspected neonatal infection, using neonatal dose tables.
questions.source_of_truth: PNG Standard Treatment Book (2016), pp. 28-31.

questions.answer: Transfuse any child with Hb <3 g/dL; at Hb 3-6 g/dL transfuse when severe infection, heart failure or kwashiorkor is present.
questions.source_of_truth: PNG Standard Treatment Book (2016), p. 18.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Outbreak definition. What is the correct action or answer?
questions.answer: An outbreak is an unexpected increase in cases above the expected baseline in a defined population and time; for some diseases one case is enough to trigger action.
questions.source_of_truth: Pacific Outbreak Manual (2016), p. 7.

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Outbreak response steps. What is the correct action or answer?

questions.question: A frontline health worker asks: Antepartum haemorrhage. What is the correct action or answer?
